title: Groupoïdes de Teichmüller et les S0 Tg,!ν, S0 TG : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, from the surrounding pages. P is a torsor over T under a bundle of connected topological groups U_T. The fibres' π_1 form a local system Π (written π here). μ is a subgroup acting freely on P, with P_0 = P/μ. C' is a fundamental groupoid (essentially Π_1(P) restricted to a set of base points). Through (21), C' is a 'π-groupoid': a groupoid with a central action of π, i.e. a homomorphism π → Aut(id_{C'}). Σ (written \mathcal{E} on the previous page) is a group receiving π; the next page has an extension 0→Π_T→Σ_T→γ_T→1. Form the change-of-band groupoid C'∧_π Σ, the pushout of the π-groupoid C' along π→Σ. This is a Σ-groupoid with the same objects, Ob(C'∧_πΣ) = Ob C' =: ε'.

Argument on this page. μ acts on Σ compatibly with its (here trivial) action on π. Hence μ acts on C'∧_πΣ by transport of structure. On objects the action is free. So the quotient set ε = ε'/μ inherits a groupoid structure: the orbit or quotient groupoid of a free action. The note 'cf. démonstration plus haut' refers back to the earlier argument, and this quotient is again a Σ-groupoid. Grothendieck concludes 'no more doubt, it is C_0'. Here C_0 is the inverse image of Π_1(P_0) over ε_0 → P_0.

Upshot: the fundamental groupoid of the quotient P_0 = P/μ is recovered purely algebraically from C' with its π-groupoid structure plus the μ-action. This is the 'construction purement algébrique' announced on the previous page. He then starts the converse ('Inversement, partons d'un Σ-groupoïde C_0 ...') and breaks off. The converse is taken up on the next page: a Σ-groupoid structure on C_0 gives a μ-covering and an extension of the torsor structure.

Purpose: in the Teichmüller-groupoid project, to pass between fundamental groupoids of torsors and of their quotients by central subgroups. Examples are quotients of Teichmüller-type spaces, or the passage from π_1 of U to π_1 of U/γ. The bookkeeping is done via central 'banded' groupoids.
errors: Gap: for the quotient of C'∧_πΣ by μ to be a Σ-groupoid with constant band Σ, μ must act on Σ in a way compatible with the central structure. Its action on morphisms must also be free and compatible. The page only says 'compatible with its (trivial) action on π'. If μ acts nontrivially on Σ, the band of the quotient would be twisted. The page does not check this; it defers to 'cf. démonstration plus haut'.
The converse direction is left unfinished on this page.

ideas.what: Groupoid with central operator group π (π → Aut id_C) and change of band C ∧_π Σ along π → Σ
ideas.modern_name: Banded / central groupoids; pushout of the band (as for gerbes)
ideas.where_published: Related banded-gerbe formalism in Giraud; not this specific form

ideas.what: Quotient of a groupoid by a group acting freely on objects recovers the fundamental groupoid of the quotient space P/μ
ideas.modern_name: Orbit groupoid / fundamental groupoid of an orbit space
ideas.usually_credited_to: R. Brown, P. J. Higgins (Topology and Groupoids; orbit groupoids, 1960s–80s)

deep.surprise_reason: A routine technical step: a quotient groupoid of a change-of-band groupoid identified with the fundamental groupoid of P/μ. It is fragmentary, with the converse unfinished, and nothing here goes beyond standard orbit-groupoid and banded-groupoid formalism.
transcription_corrections: 'ou opère librement sur Π(C'∧_πΣ)' should read 'qui opère librement sur Ob(C'∧_πΣ) = Ob C' =def ε'' (objects, not Π; a struck-out symbol precedes C').
'sur le (sens.) quotient Σ = Σ'/μ' should read 'sur l'(ens.) quotient ε = ε'/μ' (quotient set of objects, lowercase epsilon).
The marginal note reads 'cf démonstration plus haut' and attaches to 'il y a une structure de Σ-groupoïde'.
